prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal-injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, how badly you were injured, whether liability is disputed, and whether you want a law firm that will try the case in court or prefers to settle. I can, however, help you find a top attorney for your situation. Below are practical steps, criteria to use, and next actions I can take for you.

How to choose a great car-accident lawyer
- Relevant experience: look for lawyers who handle auto collisions regularly and have experience with cases like yours (catastrophic injury, wrongful death, soft-tissue claims, uninsured motorists, etc.).  
- Proven results: ask about past settlements and jury verdicts in similar cases.  
- Trial experience: a lawyer willing and able to take cases to trial usually gets better settlement offers from insurers.  
- Resources: serious cases need a firm with investigators, medical experts and the financial ability to advance costs.  
- Credentials: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law is a plus. Check AV Ratings (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, or peer reviews.  
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency is ~33% for settlement; higher if the case goes to trial. Confirm what costs you’ll owe if you lose.  
- Communication & rapport: you want someone who answers calls, explains strategy, and treats you respectfully.

Where to search and verify
- State Bar of Texas Lawyer Search (to confirm license and disciplinary history)  
- Texas Board of Legal Specialization (for board-certified personal injury trial lawyers)  
- Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Google reviews for client/peer ratings  
- Local court records for verdicts/settlements

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases do you handle per year?  
- Have you handled cases like mine? Any verdicts/settlements you can share?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? (attorney vs. paralegal)  
- What is your fee and how do you handle costs?  
- Do you take cases to trial? How often?  
- What is the expected timeline and likely outcomes?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific recovery amount.  
- Poor communication during the consultation.  
- No trial experience at all for a case that may need litigation.

Quick practical items
- Statute of limitations in Texas: generally 2 years from the date of the crash for personal injury claims — don’t wait.  
- Preserve evidence: photos, medical records, police report, contact info for witnesses.

Would you like a short list of well-rated Houston personal-injury attorneys who focus on car wrecks? If so, tell me:
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood, and  
- A brief summary of the crash (date, injury severity, whether liability is disputed).

I’ll compile a tailored shortlist and include contact info and what to ask each firm.
